THEOREM 9—Composite of Continuous Functions If ƒ is continuous at c and g is continuous at ƒ(c), then the composite g ∘ƒ is continuous at c.
Intuitively, Theorem 9 is reasonable because if x is close to c, then ƒ(x) is close to ƒ(c), and since g is continuous at ƒ(c), it follows that g(ƒ(x)) is close to g(ƒ(c)).

The continuity of composites holds for any finite number of functions. The only requirement is that each function be continuous where it is applied. For an outline of a proof of Theorem 9, see Exercise 6 in Appendix 4.
